text: Working with APIs is a common task for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually to receive or send data. Most APIs return information in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can use an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, always include error handling, because requests can fail for many reasons, and your program should respond gracefully.
